content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hey, I need a query to list customer names and their orders for a weekly report.
Happy to help! Can you confirm your table names and which columns you want from orders? Are you using Postgres, MySQL, Snowflake, or BigQuery?
I'm on Postgres. Tables are customers (id, name) and orders (id, customer_id, total_amt, created_at). I'd like customer name, order id, and total_amt.

Here's a basic query to join customers with their orders:
```sql
SELECT c.name AS customer_name, o.id AS order_id, o.total_amt
FROM customers c
INNER JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
LIMIT 10;
```
Looks good. Can we also show customers even if they have no orders?

Sure! Change INNER JOIN to LEFT JOIN to include all customers, even those without orders:
```sql
SELECT c.name AS customer_name, o.id AS order_id, o.total_amt
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
LIMIT 10;
```
How do I get only those customers who have no orders?

You can filter for NULL order IDs after the LEFT JOIN:
```sql
SELECT c.name AS customer_name
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.id IS NULL
LIMIT 10;
```
Perfect. Now, I want to see the total number of orders and total amount per customer.

Try this aggregation:
```sql
SELECT c.name AS customer_name, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count, COALESCE(SUM(o.total_amt), 0) AS total_spent
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
LIMIT 10;
```
If a customer has no orders, SUM(o.total_amt) returns NULL. COALESCE replaces NULL with 0 for better readability.
Ah, I see. Can I filter for customers who spent more than $500?

Yes, add a HAVING clause:
```sql
SELECT c.name AS customer_name, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count, COALESCE(SUM(o.total_amt), 0) AS total_spent
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
HAVING COALESCE(SUM(o.total_amt), 0) > 500
LIMIT 10;
```
What if I want to sort by the most spent?

Just add ORDER BY total_spent DESC:
```sql
SELECT c.name AS customer_name, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count, COALESCE(SUM(o.total_amt), 0) AS total_spent
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY total_spent DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
If I run into performance issues, is there a way to check how long these queries take?

In Postgres, you can prepend EXPLAIN ANALYZE to your query to see its execution plan and timing. Example:
```sql
EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT c.name AS customer_name, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count, COALESCE(SUM(o.total_amt), 0) AS total_spent
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
LIMIT 10;
```
